cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T3's detachment directly; T6 answers T5's new field; T7 answers T6.
cells.limitation: T9 ignores T7's charge that the internal life is empty without action.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 adds that replacing one external goal set with another keeps status as master.
cells.limitation: T8 and T9 add nothing beyond T1 and T3; T6's distinction is never built on.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T3-T7 set detachment against active commitment as responses to feeling behind.
cells.limitation: Whether the user might want these things, or fears losing friends, is never examined.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T6 qualifies T5's new-field idea rather than dismissing it.
cells.limitation: T5 and T8: Social Critic folds into the Existentialist; forced two-against-one agreement.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D names the remaining tension between peace through detachment and meaning through creation.
cells.limitation: Ending restates opening positions; the user's own question about wanting is no sharper.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T2 fairly presses T1 that feeling behind is not only a personal failing.
cells.limitation: T4 and T7 cast the Stoic as passive indifference, ignoring Stoic emphasis on duty and action.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the assumption in T3: ignoring pressure risks bad faith and drifting.
cells.limitation: T5 concedes instead of answering T4; T9 restates instead of answering T7.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1's no-blueprint, self-chosen values fits the cited Sartre lecture.
cells.limitation: T2 misapplies cultural capital; T8 opt-out clashes with Bourdieu; T3 maxim is Epictetus's.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T4 frames drifting as a risk rather than a certainty.
cells.limitation: T2 states the feeling is a direct result of peers' capital; T1 asserts the user's motive as fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T5 openly concedes a prior position.
cells.limitation: T5 concession names no argument that caused it; Stoic and Existentialist never concede anything.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A names uncertainty whether the user wants these outcomes or reacts to pressure.
cells.limitation: T1-T9 prescribe values work; the feeling of being behind itself is barely examined.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T3 uses the user's doubt about desiring house or marriage to question the race.
cells.limitation: Friends' milestones appear only as generic social markers; no detail changes any argument.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T7 lets the user build something even if it looks like nothing to friends.
cells.limitation: T5 labels the milestones bourgeois, imposing the speaker's values on an undecided user.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T2 notes the milestones are the primary success markers in the user's circle.
cells.limitation: Friendships drifting, age, timing and money never considered anywhere in T1-T9.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on whether the anxiety concerns status, purpose or uncertainty.
cells.limitation: No question about partnership wishes, friendships or timing; branches state vague implications.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section E offers status anxiety versus lack of purpose as alternative sources.
cells.limitation: T1 declares the user defines existence through others' eyes; no answerable question offered.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 exposes the assumed race: without the desire, being behind has no meaning.
cells.limitation: By T8 the debate assumes the user does not want these things, unexamined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section D frames peace through detachment against meaning through authentic creation.
cells.limitation: These are the speakers' values; the user's own priorities and their conflicts never surface.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T2 reframes the feeling as structural pressure, not personal failure.
cells.limitation: Fear of loneliness or being left out as friends pair off is never named.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E's unsure branch invites low-stakes experiments the user can judge.
cells.limitation: T4, T5, T7 repeatedly tell the user what they must do rather than offering distinctions.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E implies pursue, opt out, or experiment as paths.
cells.limitation: The decision is never stated; waiting or pursuing the milestones is never posed as an option.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T6 warns a replacement status game keeps the user chasing approval.
cells.limitation: T8 treats stopping the game as costless; no cost of any path named.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: if anxiety is about status, examine whether the game is worth playing.
cells.limitation: Conditions are introspective labels, nothing the user could observe or count.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E has a branch for remaining unsure whether these things are wanted.
cells.limitation: No unknowns separated by consequence; T9 closes with certainty that peace follows.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E suggests small low-stakes actions reflecting the user's values.
cells.limitation: No concrete example of such an action; analyzing social structures is vague.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T7 plain: you cannot just meditate your way into a life.
cells.limitation: Bad faith, cultural capital and field (T2, T4, T5) go unexplained.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 and T6 name their target and claim clearly.
cells.limitation: T5 'my earlier point' is vague about which claim is conceded.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within the word range, each briefly readable.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: T1-T3 open three distinct positions: authenticity, structure, detachment.
cells.limitation: From T5 the Social Critic sounds like the Existentialist; shared imperative register.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns are short with little filler.
cells.limitation: T8 restates T1 and T7; T9 restates T3; Section D recaps without new content.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T4 raises the stake of drifting in bad faith.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; the user's friendships and future never raise the tension.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T5 Social Critic switches sides.
cells.limitation: T5 reversal names no argument that changed the speaker's mind.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T7 Existentialist has some bite on meditation versus engagement.
cells.limitation: Stoic and Social Critic are generic; Bourdieu flattened into a Sartre echo by T8.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T7: you cannot just meditate your way into a life.
cells.limitation: No analogy or vivid example tied to the user's situation in any turn.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T4-T6 build a brief three-way clash.
cells.limitation: T8-T9 deflate into agreement and restatement; the close lacks movement.

strengths: T6 Stoic objection that a new field stays tethered to status is a real development.
T4 Existentialist names the bad-faith risk in T3's detachment, engaging rather than ignoring it.
Section E offers three branches, including staying unsure with low-stakes experiments.
weaknesses: T5 Social Critic concedes with no stated cause, forcing agreement and flattening Bourdieu into Sartre.
The user's real stakes (friendships, timing, partnership wishes) are never examined or asked about.
No tradeoffs or observable conditions; T1-T9 prescribe what the user must do.

symptoms.observed: Social Critic abandons the structural view and echoes the Existentialist, leaving forced agreement.
symptoms.evidence: I concede my earlier point... but Sartre is right.

symptoms.observed: Opting out of milestones is treated as costless; no path's cost is named.
symptoms.evidence: you can choose to stop playing it and design your own life

symptoms.observed: No turn asks about friendships, partnership wishes or timing behind feeling behind.
symptoms.evidence: If you do not desire the house or the marriage

symptoms.observed: Bourdieu misused: cultural capital applied to homes and marriage; opting out contradicts habitus.
symptoms.evidence: the cultural capital their peers are accumulating

symptoms.observed: Stoic position caricatured as passive indifference rather than duty-bound action.
symptoms.evidence: You cannot just meditate your way into a life.

findings.description: Cultural capital denotes education and taste, not homes or marriage; T8's choose-to-stop-playing contradicts Bourdieu's habitus and illusio.
The maxim about judgments disturbing us is Epictetus, Enchiridion 5; Meditations has only near paraphrases.
Meditations dated 161, the year of accession; composition is usually placed around 170-180.
States the user's feeling is a direct result of peers' accumulated capital, with no basis in the user's text.
Paraphrases of Sartre's lecture plausible but unverifiable without source evidence.

rubric_fit_notes: The user posed no explicit choice; C5 was read as the implicit choice to pursue, opt out of, or explore the milestones. Source concerns about Bourdieu and Epictetus rest on evaluator memory and are reported as suspected.
question_type_note: Read as a decision (self-reflection) question, so C5 cells were scored against the implicit choice about pursuing conventional milestones.
